# Summary of a 2015 UK Political Manifesto

This document outlines a comprehensive policy platform focused on national sovereignty, immigration reform, fiscal responsibility, and public service investment.

## Core Themes

The manifesto emphasizes national independence and self-governance, proposing withdrawal from the European Union as a central policy. It argues that EU membership restricts the nation's ability to control borders, negotiate trade deals, and implement domestic policies effectively. The document claims leaving the EU would save approximately £9 billion annually in direct contributions.

## Economic Policies

The fiscal approach combines tax cuts with targeted spending increases. Key proposals include:

- Raising the personal income tax allowance to £13,000
- Abolishing inheritance tax
- Creating an intermediate 30% tax rate for middle earners
- Reducing the deficit by cutting specific programmes rather than broad austerity measures
- Addressing corporate tax avoidance by large multinational companies
- Reforming the regional funding formula to create a needs-based allocation system

## Immigration

The manifesto proposes an Australian-style points-based immigration system treating all nationalities equally. It calls for a five-year moratorium on unskilled worker immigration, requiring migrants to contribute taxes for five years before accessing benefits or non-urgent healthcare. Asylum obligations under the 1951 UN Convention would be maintained.

## Public Services

Healthcare proposals include £12 billion additional NHS investment over five years, training 8,000 new GPs and 20,000 nurses, improving mental health services, and abolishing hospital parking charges. Social care funding would increase by £1.2 billion annually.

Education policies promote grammar schools, vocational training, apprenticeships, and waiving tuition fees for science and medical students who work domestically for five years post-graduation.

## Other Policy Areas

The document addresses housing shortages through brownfield development incentives, proposes defence spending increases to meet NATO commitments, supports sustainable fishing policies, and advocates for constitutional reforms including citizens' initiatives and proportional representation.
